title: try / catch
description: try/catch handles thrown errors; the catch parameter exposes .message; finally always runs. Works with async/await too.

notes: The catch binding is optional in modern JS — write `catch {}` if you do not need the error.
finally runs even when try contains return or throw — perfect for cleanup.
await unwraps a rejected promise into a thrown error — wrap awaits in try/catch to handle failures.

options: Always — even after throw or return
questions.explain: `finally` runs on the way out however the block exits — including after `try` has already evaluated its `return` value, which is why the L3 canonical logs `checked` before `42`.

questions.q: How do you read the error message inside `catch (e)`?
options: e.toString() — the only reliable way; Error has no message property
questions.explain: `new Error(msg)` sets `message` right on the error object. `toString()` also works but prefixes the name — `"SyntaxError: Unexpected token..."` — so it is not the raw text.

questions.q: How do you signal an error inside a function?
options: return new Error(...) — callers branch on `instanceof Error`
Promise.reject(new Error(...)) — the only catchable form from a sync function
Throw the message string directly: `throw "div by zero"`
questions.explain: `throw` unwinds to the nearest `catch` without the caller opting in. Returning an Error makes every call site remember to check, and throwing a bare string leaves the handler with no `.message`, `.name` or stack.

questions.q: Inside `async function f() { try { await p } catch (e) { ... } }`, when does catch run?
options: Never — rejections from an awaited promise bypass try/catch and need `.catch()`
Only if the await line itself throws a synchronous TypeError before p settles
When p resolves to an Error instance — resolved errors are auto-thrown
questions.explain: `await` rethrows a rejection at the await point, which is inside the `try`, so `catch (e)` receives the rejection reason. Resolving WITH an Error is just a normal fulfilled value — nothing is thrown.

exercises.prompt: Catch a JSON.parse error, read .message, and run a finally cleanup.
Throw your own error and recover by returning its .message.

blanks.hint: strict equality on the zero guard

L3.prompt: Write `async function loadJSON(text)` that returns the parsed .value, or "bad: " + e.name on failure. Always log "checked" in finally. Run once with `{"value":42}`, once with "oops".
hints: finally logs BEFORE the function returns its value.
Use an async IIFE to await at the top level.
e.name is "SyntaxError" — stable across engines (e.message wording is not).
